stem: Which of the following has the largest atomic radius?
solution: O, S, Se and Te all belong to Group 16. Atomic radius increases down a group as a new shell is added each period, so Te (Period 5) is the largest. Matches option D.

stem: Arrange the following in increasing order of atomic radius: F, Cl, Br, I
solution: All four are Group 17 halogens; atomic radius increases down the group, giving \(F < Cl < Br < I\). Matches option B.

stem: Which element has highest ionisation energy?
solution: He, Ne, Ar and Kr are noble gases (Group 18). Ionisation energy decreases down a group, so the smallest atom, He, has the highest ionisation energy. Matches option A.

stem: Among Li, Na, K and Rb, which has lowest ionisation energy?
solution: All are Group 1 alkali metals; ionisation energy decreases down the group, so Rb (the largest) has the lowest. Matches option D.

stem: The ionisation energy of an element increases most sharply when moving across a period. The element showing maximum increase from Na to Mg is due to
solution: Across a period the number of protons rises while electrons enter the same shell, so the greater effective nuclear charge binds the electrons more tightly and raises the ionisation energy from Na to Mg. Matches option B.

stem: The atomic radius of which pair is most nearly equal?
solution: Be and B are adjacent in Period 2 (Groups 2 and 13) and differ by only a small drop in radius (about 105 pm vs 85 pm), the closest of the listed pairs. Li and F sit at opposite ends of Period 2, while O and S differ by a whole period. Matches option B.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: Identify the group and period of the element with electronic configuration \(1s^2\,2s^2\,2p^6\,3s^2\,3p^5\).
solution: The configuration has \(Z = 17\) (chlorine). The highest principal quantum number is 3 (Period 3) and the outermost shell holds \(3s^2 3p^5 = 7\) electrons (Group 17). Matches option B.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: An element A has atomic number 20. What is its group, period, valency and valence electrons?
solution: \(Z = 20\) is calcium, \([\text{Ar}]4s^2\). The outermost shell is \(n = 4\) (Period 4) with 2 valence electrons (Group 2), which it loses to give valency 2. Matches option A.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: The electronic configuration \([\text{Ne}]\,3s^2\,3p^1\) corresponds to an element which belongs to:
solution: \([\text{Ne}]3s^2 3p^1\) is \(Z = 13\) (aluminium): the outermost shell is \(n = 3\) (Period 3), with \(3s^2 3p^1\) giving 3 valence electrons (Group 13). Matches option A.

stem: Compare the first ionisation energy (\(\text{IE}_1\)) of the following pairs:
solution: Mg has a stable filled \(3s^2\) configuration, so removing its electron needs more energy than removing the lone \(3p^1\) electron of Al; hence \(\text{IE}_1(\text{Al}) < \text{IE}_1(\text{Mg})\). Also \(\text{Si} > \text{Al}\) and \(\text{P} > \text{Si}\) (P has a stable half-filled \(3p^3\)), so options C and D are false. Matches option A.

stem: A part of the periodic table is shown below. The six elements occupy two periods: X, Y and Z lie in one period (in order, left to right across three consecutive groups), and P, Q and R lie directly beneath them in the next period (P below X, Q below Y, R below Z). Which has the largest atomic radius?
solution: Atomic radius increases down a group and increases from right to left across a period. The bottom-left position, P, is both in the lower period and the leftmost group, so it has the largest atomic radius. Matches option C.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: Which element will have 7 valence electrons and lie in period 4?
solution: Seven valence electrons means Group 17 (halogens). The Period 4 halogen is bromine (\(Z = 35\), \([\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^5\)). Cl is Period 3, F is Period 2, I is Period 5. Matches option A.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: For which of the following elements is valency not equal to the number of valence electrons?
solution: Valency equals the number of valence electrons only when that number is at most 4 (otherwise valency \(= 8 - \text{VE}\)). Na (VE 1, valency 1) is equal; Cl (VE 7, valency 1) and Ne (VE 8, valency 0) are unequal. Keyed B (Cl). Matches option B.
reviewNote: Multiple-answer defect. Official LWS key accepts b, c and d. Keyed B (Cl) for OMR. Kept PRIVATE (not a single-answer question).

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: Identify the element with electronic configuration \([\text{Ar}]\,4s^2\,4p^6\,5s^2\).
solution: The outermost shell is \(5s^2\), placing the element in Period 5, Group 2; the Group 2 element of Period 5 is strontium (\(Z = 38\), ground state \([\text{Kr}]5s^2\)). Matches option A.

stem: Which element will show anomalously high ionisation energy due to a stable half-filled configuration?
solution: A half-filled p-subshell (\(p^3\)) is extra-stable, raising the ionisation energy above its neighbour. Nitrogen (\(2p^3\)) shows this anomaly (\(\text{IE: N} > \text{O}\)). (Phosphorus, \(3p^3\), shows the same effect.) Matches option A.
reviewNote: Multiple-correct defect: both N (\(2p^3\)) and P (\(3p^3\)) are half-filled. Official LWS key is a (N). Kept PRIVATE (P is also chemically valid).

stem: The correct order of ionisation energy for the following is:
solution: Actual first ionisation energies (kJ/mol): Al 578, Mg 738, Si 786, P 1012, giving \(Al < Mg < Si < P\). The printed options omit this order; option A (\(Mg < Al < Si < P\)) is the simple left-to-right period trend and is keyed as the intended answer. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Correct-answer-absent defect: the true order \(Al < Mg < Si < P\) is not an option. Official LWS key is a, with the teacher noting only Mg should be ahead of Al. Keyed A. Kept PRIVATE.

stem: Consider the elements A (\(Z = 11\)), B (\(Z = 12\)), C (\(Z = 17\)), D (\(Z = 19\)). Which has greatest atomic radius?
solution: A = Na, B = Mg, C = Cl (all Period 3) and D = K (Period 4, Group 1). Atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period, so K (Period 4, leftmost group) is the largest. Matches option D.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: Which of the following has an electronic configuration corresponding to a noble gas?
solution: Option A is Cl (\(Z = 17\)) and option D is Na (\(Z = 11\)). Option B, \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\), is neon (\(Z = 10\)), and option C, ending \(3s^2 3p^6\), is argon (\(Z = 18\)) — both noble gases. The official LWS key is B (neon). Matches option B.
reviewNote: Multiple-correct defect: both B (\(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\) = Ne) and C (ending \(3s^2 3p^6\) = Ar) are noble gases. Official LWS key is b (Ne). Kept PRIVATE (Ar is also valid).

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: Identify the period of an element with configuration \([\text{Kr}]\,5s^2\,4d^{10}\,5p^3\).
solution: The highest principal quantum number in the configuration is 5 (\(5s, 5p\)), so the element lies in Period 5 (it is antimony, \(Z = 51\)). Matches option B.

stem: Which statement is true for ionisation energy across a period?
solution: Across a period the nuclear charge rises and the atomic radius falls, so electrons are held more tightly and the ionisation energy increases (apart from minor anomalies). Matches option B.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: Find the valency and valence electrons of phosphorus (\(Z = 15\)).
solution: Phosphorus is \([\text{Ne}]3s^2 3p^3\), so it has 5 valence electrons. Being in Group 15, its common valency is \(8 - 5 = 3\) (as in \(\text{PH}_3\)). Matches option A.

stem: In the sequence Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, which element has minimum atomic radius?
solution: All five are Period 3 elements; atomic radius decreases left to right across a period as nuclear charge increases, so phosphorus (rightmost) has the minimum radius. Matches option D.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: An element X has 3 shells and 6 valence electrons. Identify its possible group and period.
solution: Three occupied shells means Period 3; 6 valence electrons means Group 16. The element is sulphur (\(Z = 16\)). Matches option A.

stem: Choose the correct order of decreasing atomic radius for the following:
solution: O, S, Se and Te are Group 16 elements; atomic radius increases down the group, so the decreasing order is \(Te > Se > S > O\). Matches option B.

subtopic: Position in Periodic Table and Electronic Configuration
stem: The electronic configuration of an element is \([\text{Ne}]\,3s^2\,3p^6\,3d^1\). Find its group, period and valency.
solution: A \(3d^1\) outer electron places the element in the d-block, Period 4, Group 3 (scandium, \([\text{Ar}]3d^1 4s^2\), valency 3). Option A gives the correct Group 3 and Period 4 (its stated valency 2 is inexact). Matches option A.
reviewNote: Broken question (teacher: 'wrong data, not match'): \([\text{Ne}]3s^2 3p^6 3d^1\) is not a valid ground-state config and no option fully matches. Keyed A (best group+period). Kept PRIVATE.
